confirmed.statement: S1 analyzed 203 distinct MBA and EMBA students; 957 is their conversation count, not a count of people.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 2, Approach, final sentence; p. 10, Supporting Information, Descriptive Statistics of the Study Sample.

confirmed.statement: The participant flow is 224 initial students, minus 17 who did not use the required modalities, minus 4 with insufficient data for adjusted diversity measures, leaving 203; these are not reported randomized-enrollment counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Supporting Information, Sample Preprocessing.

confirmed.statement: Voice and text account for 458 and 499 analyzed conversations, respectively. Table 1 calls these users, but Figure 1 and the appendix explicitly identify the same totals as conversations; the form correctly avoids entering them as arm-level people counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Figure 1 caption; p. 9, Table 1 notes; p. 10, Descriptive Statistics of the Study Sample.

confirmed.statement: The female-voice and male-voice counts are 240 and 218 conversations, summing to the 458 voice conversations. They are nested conditions in the same dataset, not additional independent samples.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, first paragraph; p. 10, Descriptive Statistics of the Study Sample.

confirmed.statement: The PDF does not supply exact distinct-person totals randomized or analyzed in each modality or voice-gender arm, or the distinct-person total initially randomized to voice gender. The corresponding null fields in the form are appropriate.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 3 and 5, voice-gender assignment and finding; pp. 8-10, figure, table and sample descriptions; full Supporting Information, pp. 10-16.

confirmed.statement: Of the 203 analyzed users, 186 used both modalities. Consequently the voice and text groups overlap extensively and their participant totals cannot be added as independent samples.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, second paragraph: 92% of users (186 of 203) utilized both modalities over the term.

confirmed.statement: Derived lower bound: at least 186 distinct analyzed people contributed voice conversations, because 186 of the 203 analyzed users used both modalities. All 458 analytic voice conversations are accounted for by the two randomly assigned voice genders, and the paper reports analyzing voice-gender effects; this supports the 50-person threshold for that nested comparison without inventing exact arm counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, random voice-gender assignment and 186-of-203 overlap; p. 5, Findings, final paragraph; p. 10, Descriptive Statistics of the Study Sample, analytic voice-gender counts.

confirmed.statement: Voice versus text was self-selected. The randomized factor is perceived AI voice gender within spoken interactions; the sample-size finding does not make the principal modality comparison randomized.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, first two paragraphs; p. 6, Discussion, limitations; p. 10, Modality Switching Across Successive CAiSEY Sessions.

confirmed.statement: The 754 admissible transitions and 398 switches count repeated session pairs and switching events, not extra participants. Excluding each user's first session from the transition calculation is not an additional participant exclusion.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Modality Switching Across Successive CAiSEY Sessions.

confirmed.statement: Text preprocessing also excludes short texts or chunks and assigns missing values to some semantic-diversity calculations. No additional distinct-person attrition count or exclusions by voice-gender arm are supplied, so these rules cannot be converted into extra people counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Content Originality and Divergent Ideation; p. 12, continuation of Divergent Ideation; p. 10, Sample Preprocessing.

confirmed.statement: Only one student dataset is described; the voice-gender comparison reuses its spoken interactions. No reuse of participants from another paper is disclosed, supporting the form's cross-paper overlap value of not_stated rather than a claim of independence.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 2-3, Approach; p. 10, sample description; full document and Supporting Information, pp. 1-16.

summary: The PDF supports 203 analyzed people after 17 and 4 exclusions from 224, and the form correctly distinguishes people from conversations. The randomized voice-gender subset contains at least 186 people by the reported modality overlap, so the 50-person threshold holds, although exact gender-arm counts are unreported and the main modality comparison is observational.
